nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Of that is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يسۤن. وَٱلْقُرْآنِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾.
ʿĪsā [ibn ʿUmar] read ﴿يَاسِينَ﴾ with fatḥa on the nūn.
Sufyān related from Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī, from al-Ḥusayn: ﴿يسۤ﴾ — he said: an opening of the Qurʾān. [Translator's note: the source has «الحسين»; the parallel narration below is from al-Ḥasan.]
Hushaym related from Ḥuṣayn, from al-Ḥasan, who said: ﴿يَسِ﴾ — he said: "O human being"; and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said the same.
ʿIkrima said: it is an oath.
Mujāhid said: it is one of the openings of the speech of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.
Qatāda said: it is a name of the sūra.
The reading of ʿĪsā may be taken as a name of the sūra, made accusative (manṣūb) by an implied verb.
And the fatḥa may be for the meeting of two sukūns. [Translator's note: the source has «لالتفاء», a misprint for «لالتقاء» "meeting".]
Sībawayh said: some read ﴿يَسنَ. والقرآنَ﴾ and ﴿قَ. والقرآنَ﴾ — meaning with both in the accusative.
He said: whoever says this has, as it were, made it a foreign name, then said: "Mention Yāsīn."
Abū Jaʿfar said: this indicates that Sībawayh's position on "يس" is that it is the name of the sūra, as Qatāda said.
Sībawayh said: it is also possible that ﴿يس﴾ and ﴿صاد﴾ are two non-declinable (ghayr mutamakkin) nouns, so that the fatḥa is fixed on them, just as fixed vowels are imposed on non-declinable nouns such as "كَيْفَ، وَأَيْنَ، وحَيْثُ، وأَمْسِ".

nahhas-meani:3-4.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّكَ لَمِنَ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ. عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ [verses 3 and 4].
A khabar (predicate) after a khabar.
And it is possible that ﴿عَلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾ belongs to the ṣila (complement) of "the messengers", i.e. "you are of those sent upon uprightness in the truth".

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿تَنزِيلَ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلرَّحِيمِ﴾.
That is, what has been revealed to you is a sending-down of the Mighty, the Merciful.
And the accusative is because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun).

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لِتُنذِرَ قَوْماً مَّآ أُنذِرَ آبَآؤُهُمْ فَهُمْ غَافِلُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: some said: "that you may warn a people to whose fathers no warner came before you."
And some said: "that you may warn a people the like of what their fathers were warned."
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning according to the second view is: that you may warn a people with what their fathers were warned with, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿فَقُلْ أَنْذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً﴾. [Translator's note: the source has a stray «إ» before «المعنى».]

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لَقَدْ حَقَّ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَىٰ أَكْثَرِهِمْ فَهُمْ لاَ يُؤمِنُونَ﴾.
That is, the word became binding upon them because of their unbelief, that the Fire is theirs.
And it has been said: as a punishment for their unbelief.

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِنَّا جَعَلْنَا فِيۤ أَعْناقِهِمْ أَغْلاَلاً﴾.
There are several views on the meaning of this:
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: We prevented them from spending in the way of Allah, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَلاَ تَجْعَلْ يَدَكَ مَغْلُولَةً إلَى عُنُقِكَ﴾.
And it has been said: this is on the Day of Resurrection, when they enter the Fire.
And the past tense is in the sense of the future, or [it is past] because Allah, Majestic and Mighty, has announced it.
Or it is on the implication of "when it comes to be" (idhā kāna).
And it has been said: "We made" means "We described them as being so".
Sībawayh reported that "جَعَلَ" comes in the speech of the Arabs with this meaning; this is one of his views on their saying "جَعَلتَ متَاعَك بعضَه فوقَ بعض" (you made / considered your goods, some of them on top of others), and on His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا المَلائِكَةَ الَّذِينَ هُمْ عِبَادُ الرَّحْمَنِ إنَاثَاً﴾.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَهِىَ إِلَى ٱلأَذْقَانِ فَهُم مُّقْمَحُونَ﴾.
The meaning is: so their hands are up to the chins. The hands had not been mentioned, because the meaning is understood, as [the poet] said:
فَمَا أَدْرِي إذَا يَمَّمْتُ وَجْهَاً * أُرِيدُ الخَيْرَ أَيّهمَا يَلِيِني
أَأَلْخَيرُ الَّذِي أَنَا أَبْتَغِيهِ * أَمِ الشَرُّ الَّذِي لا يَأْتَلِيني
(I do not know, when I set out in some direction seeking good, which of the two will befall me: the good that I seek, or the evil that does not fail to reach me — "the two" refers to good and evil, though only good had been mentioned.)
And in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿إنَّا جَعَلْنَا في أَيْمَانِهِمْ أَغْلاَلاً﴾.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَهُم مُّقْمَحُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, raising their heads, with their hands over their mouths.
Al-Farrāʾ said: it is one who raises his head and lowers his gaze.
Abū ʿUbayda said: it is one who is pulled, while raising his head.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what is known in the language is that «المُقْمح» is one who raises his head because of something disagreeable. From it the two months of Kānūn are called "the two months of qimāḥ", because when the camels come to water in them, they raise their heads from the cold. And from it is [the poet's] saying:
وَنَحنُ عَلَى جَوانِبِها قُعُوْدٌ * نَغُضُّ الطَّرْفَ كَالإبِلِ القِمَاح
(And we sit around its sides, lowering our gaze like camels that raise their heads from the water.)

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا مِن بَيْنِ أَيْدِيهِمْ سَدّاً ومِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ سَدّاً﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-sadd and al-sudd: the mountain [i.e. barrier]. The meaning is: We blinded them, as [the poet] said:
وَمِنَ الحَوَادِثِ ـ لا أَبَالَكِ ـ أَنَّني * ضَرَبتْ عَليَّ الأرضُ بالأَسْــدَادِ
لاَ أَهْتَدِي فِيهَا لِمَوْضِع تَلْعَةٍ * بينَ العُذَيْبِ وَبَيْنَ أَرْضِ مُرَادِ
(Among misfortunes — may you have no father! — is that the earth has been walled off for me with barriers; I cannot find my way in it to the place of a single watercourse between al-ʿUdhayb and the land of Murād.)
ʿIkrima said: whatever is of Allah's making, Mighty and Majestic, is sadd, and whatever is of the making of creatures is sudd.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq said: whatever is not seen is sadd, and whatever is seen is sudd.
It is related that they intended harm to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, came between them and him; that is, it became as though there were a barrier between them and him, and as though there were fetters on their necks. So said ʿIkrima, and it was revealed about Abū Jahl.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَأغْشَيْنَاهُمْ فَهُمْ لاَ يُبْصِرُونَ﴾.
Al-taghshiya is covering. It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās and ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz [that they read] ﴿فَأعْشَيْنَاهُمْ﴾ with the undotted ʿayn, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَنْ يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطَانَاً فَهُوَ لَهُ قَرِينٌ﴾.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّا نَحْنُ نُحْيِي ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَنَكْتُبُ مَاَ قَدَّمُواْ وَآثَارَهُمْ﴾.
Simāk related from ʿIkrima from Ibn ʿAbbās: "The Anṣār were far from the mosque, so they said: Let us take places close to the mosque. Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed ﴿وَنَكْتُبُ مَاَ قَدَّمُواْ وَآثَارَهُمْ﴾, and they said: We will stay in our place."
Masrūq said: there is no man who takes a step but Allah records for him a good deed or a bad deed.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: ﴿آثَارَهُمْ﴾: their footsteps.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿نَكْتُبُ مَاَ قَدَّمُواْ﴾: their deeds; and ﴿آثَارَهُمْ﴾: what [practices] they established that continued after them.

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱضْرِبْ لَهُمْ مَّثَلاً أَصْحَابَ ٱلقَرْيَةِ إِذْ جَآءَهَا ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾.
ʿIkrima said: it is Antioch.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "I have ḍurūb of this", i.e. likenesses.
So the meaning on this basis is: and set forth for them a likeness, i.e. mention to them a likeness, ﴿أَصْحَابَ ٱلقَرْيَةِ﴾ as a badal (substitute), i.e. mention the people of the town.
And the meaning is: and mention the story of the people of the town when the messengers came to it.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِذْ أَرْسَلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱثْنَيْنِ فَكَذَّبُوهُمَا فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: Jesus ﷺ sent to them two of the disciples, and they denied them.
Kaʿb and Wahb said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty, sent to "Anṭīkhus", the pharaoh at Antioch — who worshipped idols — two [messengers], then reinforced them with a third.
Al-Farrāʾ said: the third was sent before the two, while in the recitation it is as though he was sent after them. He said: the meaning of ﴿فَعَزَّزْنَا بِثَالِثٍ﴾ is: We reinforced [them] by the teaching of the third.
He said: and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: "فعزَّزنا بالثَّالثِ". The people of tafsīr hold the opposite of his view, and his view is not evident — and Allah knows best.
Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: ﴿فَعَزَّزْنَا﴾: We strengthened.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ʿĀṣim read ﴿فَعَزَزْنَا﴾ without doubling; he said: it is like shadadnā and shaddadnā.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what is known in the language is that the meaning of "عَزَزْنَا" is "we overcame and subdued", and its imperfect is on the pattern "yafʿulu", with ḍamma.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قَالُوۤاْ إِنَّا تَطَيَّرْنَا بِكُمْ لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, whatever evil befalls us is because of you.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿لَئِن لَّمْ تَنتَهُواْ لَنَرْجُمَنَّكُمْ﴾ — that is, we shall surely kill you by stoning.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قَالُواْ طَائِرُكُم مَّعَكُمْ أَئِن ذُكِّرْتُم بَلْ أَنتُمْ قَوْمٌ مُّسْرِفُونَ﴾.
It is related from Mujāhid from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: ﴿طَائِرُكُم مَّعَكُمْ﴾ — that is, provisions and decrees follow you.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and of this is His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَكُلَّ إنْسَانٍ أَلْزَمْنَاهُ طَائِرَهُ في عُنُقِهِ﴾ — that is, whatever good and evil "flies" to him is bound to his neck, by way of figurative likeness.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَئِن ذُكِّرْتُم﴾. Qatāda said: that is, "if you are reminded, do you draw evil omens?"
Abū Razīn read ﴿أَأَنْ ذُكّرْتُمْ﴾.
The meaning according to his reading is: is it because you were reminded of Allah, or of the punishment, that you draw evil omens?
ʿĪsā read: ﴿قَالُوا طَائِركُمْ مَعَكُمْ أَيِنَ ذُكِّرْتُمْ﴾.
And al-Ḥasan read: ﴿أَيْنَ ذُكِّرْتُمْ﴾, and explained it: wherever you are reminded, your omen is with you.

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَجَآءَ مِنْ أَقْصَى ٱلْمَدِينَةِ رَجُلٌ يَسْعَىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said: he is "Ḥabīb the carpenter".
Qatāda said: he used to worship Allah, Majestic and Mighty, in a cave. When he heard the news of the messengers, [he came hurrying and said to the messengers: Do you ask any wage for what you have brought? They said: No, our wage is only with Allah. So he said: O my people, follow the messengers] up to His saying ﴿إِنِّي آمَنْتُ بِرَبِّكُمْ فَاسْمَعُونَ﴾ — he said this to the messengers.
Kaʿb and Wahb said: he said this to his people.
Qatāda said: then his people stoned him, and he said: "O Allah, guide my people" — I think he said — "for they do not know." They kept stoning him until they killed him on the spot; and Allah, Majestic and Mighty, admitted him into Paradise, and Allah did not grant his people respite until He destroyed them.
Kaʿb and Wahb said: they leapt upon him as one man and killed him, and then, behold, they were extinguished.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قِيلَ ٱدْخُلِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ قَالَ يٰلَيْتَ قَوْمِي يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قِيلَ ٱدْخُلِ ٱلْجَنَّةَ﴾: it was said to him: Paradise is due to you.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِن كَانَتْ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar [the reader] read ﴿إِن كَانَتْ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ﴾.
The meaning according to his reading: their punishment occurred as nothing but a single shout. ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ خَامِدُونَ﴾ — that is, still, like extinguished ashes.

nahhas-meani:30-30.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿يٰحَسْرَةً عَلَى ٱلْعِبَادِ مَا يَأْتِيهِمْ مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلاَّ كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِئُونَ﴾.
In the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy: ﴿يَا حَسْرَةَ العِباَدِ﴾ — that is, this is the occasion for regret to be present.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the true sense of ḥasra (regret) in the language is that remorse overtakes a person to the point that he becomes exhausted (ḥasīr) by it.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إِلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
Sībawayh said: it [i.e. «أنهم»] is a badal (substitute) for "كَمْ", i.e. "Have they not seen that the generations whom We destroyed — that they do not return?!"
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: this is not sound and not permissible. The meaning of ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ﴾ is "have they not known?", because they were only informed of this; and ﴿كَمْ﴾ is accusative by ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا﴾.
The meaning is: have they not known how many generations We destroyed before them? That is, by the fact that they do not return to them, i.e. by extermination.
He said: the evidence for this is that in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd it is ﴿مَنْ أَهْلَكْنَا قَبْلَهُمْ مِنَ القُرُونِ أَنَّهُمْ إلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
And al-Ḥasan read: ﴿إِنَّهُمْ إلَيْهِمْ لاَ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:32-32.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن كُلٌّ لَّمَّا جَمِيعٌ لَّدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ﴾.
"إنْ" is in the sense of "ما" (not), and "لَمَّا" is in the sense of "إلاَّ" (except).
The grammarians report: "باللهِ لَمَّا قمتَ" (by Allah, you must stand), in the sense of "إلاَّ".
And in the reading of Ubayy ibn Kaʿb: ﴿وَإنْ منهُمْ إلاَّ جَمِيعٌ لَدَيْنَا مُحْضَرُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ ٱلأَرْضُ ٱلْمَيْتَةُ أَحْيَيْنَاهَا﴾.
That is, and a sign that points to the power of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and to His giving life to the dead, is the dead earth: We gave it life.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِيَأْكُلُواْ مِن ثَمَرِهِ وَمَا عَمِلَتْهُ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: that is, and their hands did not make it [taking «ما» as negative].
And it is read ﴿وَمَا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾, meaning: and that which their hands made.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿سُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَق ٱلأَزْوَاجَ كُلَّهَا﴾.
That is, the kinds of fruits, animals and other things.

nahhas-meani:37-37.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمُ ٱلْلَّيْلُ نَسْلَخُ مِنْهُ ٱلنَّهَارَ فَإِذَا هُم مُّظْلِمُونَ﴾.
One says "I stripped (salakhtu) the thing from the thing", i.e. I removed it from it and separated it until nothing of it remained. ﴿فَإِذَا هُم مُّظْلِمُونَ﴾.
﴿فَإِذَا هُم مُّظْلِمُونَ﴾: that is, entering into darkness.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَّهَـا ذَلِكَ تَقْدِيرُ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْعَلِيمِ﴾.
It has been said that the meaning is: to the place of its resting, as has come in the ḥadīth: (It goes and prostrates before its Lord, Majestic and Mighty; then it asks permission to return, and permission is given to it...).
That is: and a sign for them is the sun, running to a resting place of its own. [Translator's note: the source has «آي», read as «أي» "that is".]
And it may be that it [al-shams] is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and ﴿لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَّهَـا﴾ the khabar (predicate), i.e. for a term of its own.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he read ﴿لاَ مُسْتَقَرَّ لَهَا﴾, i.e. running, not staying fixed in one place.
Al-Aʿmash related from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from his father, from Abū Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: (I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلشَّمْسُ تَجْرِي لِمُسْتَقَرٍّ لَّهَـا﴾. He said: Its resting place is beneath the Throne.)
And it has been said: [it runs] to the farthest of its stations in setting, then returns and does not go beyond it.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱلْقَمَرَ قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَٱلعُرجُونِ ٱلْقَدِيمِ﴾.
That is, and a sign for them is the moon.
And it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject), with the khabar (predicate) being ﴿قَدَّرْنَاهُ مَنَازِلَ﴾, and the implied form being:
"We measured it out as having stations", as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَإذَا كَالُوهُم﴾, i.e. "measured for them".
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَٱلعُرجُونِ ٱلْقَدِيمِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, like the dried, bent date-stalk (ʿidhq) of the palm.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what Qatāda said is what the lexicographers report. Al-ʿidhq, with kasra on the ʿayn, is the kibāsa and the qinw (the fruit-bunch stalk); the people of Egypt call it al-isbāṭa. When it dries, the moon at the end and the beginning of the month is likened to it.
And al-ʿadhq, with fatḥa on the ʿayn, is the palm tree.

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿لاَ ٱلشَّمْسُ يَنبَغِي لَهَآ أَن تدْرِكَ ٱلقَمَرَ وَلاَ ٱلْلَّيْلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, the sun does not come so that its light overpowers the light of the moon, nor does the moon rise so that its light mixes with the light of the sun. ﴿وَلاَ ٱلْلَّيْلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِ﴾ — he said: that is, it does not depart before the day comes.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَكُلٌّ فِي فَلَكٍ يَسْبَحُونَ﴾.
Everything that moves with a gliding, outspread movement is "swimming" (sābiḥ).

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَآيَةٌ لَّهُمْ أَنَّا حَمَلْنَا ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ فِي ٱلْفُلْكِ ٱلْمَشْحُونِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best of what has been said about this is that the meaning is: and a sign for the people of Mecca is that We carried the offspring of the past generations in the laden ship.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَخَلَقْنَا لَهُمْ مِّن مِّثْلِهِ مَا يَرْكَبُونَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū Mālik, Abū Ṣāliḥ and al-Ḥasan said: it means ships.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Shaddād ibn al-Hād, ʿIkrima, Mujāhid and Qatāda said: it means camels.
Abū Jaʿfar said: camels and riding animals on land are like ships at sea; yet the first is closer to the interpretation of it, because of the indication of His saying ﴿وَإنْ نَشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ﴾, and drowning is only in water.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِن نَّشَأْ نُغْرِقْهُمْ فَلاَ صَرِيخَ لَهُمْ وَلاَ هُمْ يُنقَذُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, then there is no rescuer for them.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمُ ٱتَّقُواْ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, what is before you of the calamities that befell those before you; ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ﴾ — he said: of the Hereafter.
The meaning according to al-Ḥakam ibn ʿUtayba: ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ of this world, i.e. the like of what befell ʿĀd and Thamūd; ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ﴾: the Hereafter.
According to Mujāhid: ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ of your sins, and what you did not know.
According to Ibn ʿAbbās and Saʿīd ibn Jubayr: ﴿مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيكُمْ﴾ is the Hereafter and ﴿وَمَا خَلْفَكُمْ﴾ this world; and they said the same about the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ثُمَّ لآتِيَنَّهُمْ مِنْ بَيْنِ أَيْديهِمْ وَمِنْ خَلْفِهِمْ﴾.
The implied construction in Arabic is: "And when it is said to them: fear what is before you and what is behind you, they turn away."
This omission is indicated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا تَأْتِيهِمْ مِنْ آيَةٍ مِنْ آيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ إلاَّ كَانُوا عَنْهَا مُعْرِضِينَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ أَنفِقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱلله﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: they are the Jews.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ أَنُطْعِمُ مَن لَّوْ يَشَآءُ ٱللَّهُ أَطْعَمَهُ﴾.
They say this mockingly.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مَا يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً تَأْخُذُهُمْ وَهُمْ يَخِصِّمُونَ﴾.
In the reading of Ubayy: ﴿وهم يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾, and the meaning is the same.
And it is read ﴿يَخْصِمُونَ﴾, i.e. some of them dispute with others.
And its meaning may be: and they, in their own estimation, are defeating with argument those who believe in the Hour.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿فَلاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ تَوْصِيَةً وَلاَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾.
That is, they are not given respite so that they could make bequests.
﴿وَلاَ إِلَىٰ أَهْلِهِمْ يَرْجِعُونَ﴾: that is, they die where they are.
And the meaning may be: nor do they return a word to their families.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: it is the plural of ṣūra (form).
He holds that the meaning is: and [breath] was blown into the bodies, and he cited as evidence the saying of the poet:
لَمَّا أَتَى خَبَرُ الزُّبَيْرِ تَوَاضَعَتْ * سُورُ المَدِينَةِ وَالجِبَالُ الخُشَّعُ
(When the news of al-Zubayr came, the walls of the city and the humbled mountains bowed low.)
Abū Jaʿfar said: what Abū ʿUbayda said is not recognised by the people of tafsīr nor by the people of language.
The ḥadīth is that it is the trumpet (ṣūr) into which Isrāfīl, Allah's blessing be upon him, blows.
And the lexicographers hold that the plural of "ṣūra" is ṣuwar.
And Sībawayh and others hold that sūr al-madīna (the city wall) is not the plural of sūra.
* Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿إِذَا هُم مِّنَ ٱلأَجْدَاثِ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنسِلُونَ﴾.
That is, the graves. The grave is called jadath and jadaf.
﴿لَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ يَنسِلُونَ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source, for «إلى ربهم ينسلون».] Abū ʿUbayda said: that is, they hasten.

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰوَيْلَنَا مَن بَعَثَنَا مِن مَّرْقَدِنَا﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿مَنْ أَهَبَّنَا مِنْ مرقدنا﴾.
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said: they sleep a sleep before the Resurrection [and find rest in it, so they say: Woe to us! Who has raised us from our sleeping-place?].
Al-Aʿmash said: it has reached me that the punishment is withheld from them between the two blasts; then when the trumpet is blown they say: Who has raised us from our sleeping-place?
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: this is the saying of the unbelievers, and the believers said to them: ﴿هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ ٱلرَّحْمـٰنُ وَصَدَقَ ٱلْمُرْسَلُونَ﴾.
And it has been said: this is what the angels say to them.
And it has been said: the full stop is at His saying ﴿هَذَا﴾.
And the meaning [then] is: what the All-Merciful promised is true.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿إِنَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْجَنَّةِ ٱليَوْمَ فِي شُغُلٍ فَاكِهُونَ﴾.
One says "so-and-so is fākih", i.e. possessor of fruit, and "tāmir", i.e. possessor of dates, as the poet said:
أَغَرَرْتَنِي وَزَعَمْتَ انَّكَ * لاَبِنٌ بِالصَّيْفِ تَامِرٌ
(Did you deceive me, claiming that you are, in summer, a possessor of milk and dates?)
Ibn Abī Ṭalḥa related from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿فَاكِهِينَ﴾: rejoicing.
And in some tafsīrs: living in comfort.
As for ﴿فَكِهُونَ﴾, al-Farrāʾ said: its meaning is like the meaning of fākihīn, as one says ḥadhir and ḥādhir; and this is the most fitting of them.
Abū Zayd said: one says a man is fakih when he is good-humoured and much given to laughter.
Abū ʿUbayda said: one says he is fakih with food, or with fruit, or with people's reputations.
Qatāda said: ﴿فَكِهُونَ﴾: delighted.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿هُمْ وَأَزْوَاجُهُمْ فِي ظِلاَلٍ عَلَى ٱلأَرَآئِكِ مُتَّكِئُونَ﴾.
﴿فِي ظِلاَلٍ﴾ is the plural of ẓill (shade).
And it may be the plural of ẓulla (canopy); as for "ẓulal", it is the plural of ẓulla and nothing else.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatāda said: ﴿الأَرَائِكُ﴾ are couches within curtained alcoves (ḥijāl).
And it has been said: the furnishings within curtained alcoves.
And it has been said: they are furnishings wherever they may be; this is known in the speech of the Arabs. Dhū al-Rumma said:
خُدُوْدَاً جَفَتْ في السَّيْرِ حَتَّى كأنَّما * يُبَاشِرْنَ بِالمَعْزَاءِ مَسَّ الأَرائِكِ
(Cheeks that have grown hardened in travel, until it is as though, on the stony ground, they were touching the softness of cushions.)

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لَهُمْ فِيهَا فَاكِهَةٌ وَلَهُمْ مَّا يَدَّعُونَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: that is, what they wish for. One says "iddaʿ ʿalayya mā shiʾta", i.e. wish [for whatever you like].
Abū Jaʿfar said: it is taken from calling (duʿāʾ) for a thing, i.e. whenever they call for something they are given it.

nahhas-meani:58-58.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿سَلاَمٌ قَوْلاً مِّن رَّبٍّ رَّحِيمٍ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ said: that is, that is theirs, peace, i.e. secured [from harm].
Abū Isḥāq said: ﴿سلامٌ﴾ is a badal (substitute) for ﴿مَا﴾, i.e. and theirs is that Allah, Majestic and Mighty, greets them with peace — and that is the utmost of their wishes.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿سَلاَماً﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: ﴿قَوْلاً﴾ — that is, Allah says that greeting of peace as a saying [Translator's note: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)].
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning may be: and theirs is whatever they call for, as a word [of promise], as you say "as a promise" (ʿidatan).

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَٱمْتَازُواْ ٱلْيَوْمَ أَيُّهَا ٱلْمُجْرِمُونَ﴾.
That is, separate yourselves from the believers. One says: miztuhu fa-nmāza and imtāza (I separated it and it became separate), and mayyaztuhu fa-tamayyaza.

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَلَمْ أَعْهَدْ إِلَيْكُمْ يٰبَنِيۤ ءَادَمَ أَن لاَّ تَعْبُدُواْ ٱلشَّيطَانَ﴾.
That is: did I not give you prior notice and enjoin you?!

nahhas-meani:62-62.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنْكُمْ جِبِلاًّ كَثِيراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, a creation (multitude).
Abū Jaʿfar said: there are seven forms of it, five of which have been read.
The five which have been read are: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَضَلَّ مِنْكُمْ جِبِلاًّ﴾, ﴿جِبْلاً﴾, ﴿جُبُلاً﴾, ﴿جُبْلاً﴾ and ﴿جَبْلاً﴾.
And the two which have not been read are "جُبَلاً" and "جِبَلاً".

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱلْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَىٰ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ وَتُكَلِّمُنَآ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: ﴿الْيَوْمَ نَخْتِمُ عَلَى أَفْواهِهِمْ وَلِتُكَلِّمَنَا أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
On this reading there is an omission in the speech, as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُرِي إبْرَاهيمَ مَلَكُوتَ السَّمَوَاتِ والأَرْضَ وَلِيَكُونَ مِنَ المُوْقِنِينِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَطَمَسْنَا عَلَىٰ أَعْيُنِهِمْ فَٱسْتَبَقُواْ ٱلصِّرَاطَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: that is, We would have left them blind, wandering to and fro.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-maṭmūs and al-ṭamīs, according to the lexicographers, is the blind person who has no slit in his eyes.
﴿فَٱسْتَبَقُواْ ٱلصِّرَاطَ﴾: that is, so as to pass over.
Mujāhid said: ﴿الصِّرَاطُ﴾ is the road.
* Then He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَأَنَّىٰ يُبْصِرُونَ﴾ — that is, then from where would they see?

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿وَلَوْ نَشَآءُ لَمَسَخْنَاهُمْ عَلَىٰ مَكَـانَتِهِمْ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: that is, We would have crippled them (made them sit).
And from Ibn ʿAbbās, he said: that is, if We willed, We would have destroyed them in their dwellings.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-makān and al-makāna are the same.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَن نُّعَمِّرْهُ نُنَكِّـسْهُ فِي ٱلْخَلْقِ أَفَلاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: it is decrepitude: his hearing, his sight and his strength change, as you have seen.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿وَمَا عَلَّمْنَاهُ ٱلشِّعْرَ وَمَا يَنبَغِي لَهُ﴾.
That is, it is not fitting that he should compose it.
Abū Isḥāq said: this does not entail that the Prophet ﷺ never quoted a line of poetry; rather it entails that he ﷺ is not a poet, and that the Qurʾān does not resemble poetry.
Qatāda said: it has reached me that ʿĀʾisha said: the Prophet ﷺ never quoted a line of poetry except the line of Ṭarafa:
سَتُبْدِي لَكَ الأَيَّامُ ما كُنْتَ جَاهِلاً * ويَأْتِيكَ بَالأَخْبَارِ مَنْ لَمْ تُزَوِّدِ
(The days will reveal to you what you did not know, and one whom you did not provision will bring you the news.)
And he said: "and one whom you did not provision will bring you the news" [reversing the word order].
Abū Bakr said: it is not like that, O Messenger of Allah.
He said: I am not good at poetry, and it is not fitting for me.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لِّيُنذِرَ مَن كَانَ حَيّاً وَيَحِقَّ ٱلْقَوْلُ عَلَى ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
﴿حَيَّاً﴾: it has been said: possessed of reason.
And it has been said: a believer.
And Qatāda said: alive of heart.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَا لَهُم مِمَّا عَمِلَتْ أَيْدِينَآ أَنْعاماً﴾.
The Arabs use "hand" in place of "power"; and Allah knows best what He intended.
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَهُمْ لَهَا مَالِكُونَ﴾.
That is, they have control [of them], because what is intended here is subjugation [of the animals]. Sībawayh recited:
أَصْبَحْتُ لاَ أَمْلِكُ السِّلاَحَ وَلاَ * أَمْلِكُ رَأْسَ البَعير إنْ نَفَرَا
(I have become one who cannot manage a weapon, nor control the camel's head if it bolts.)

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَطِيعُونَ نَصْرَهُمْ وَهُمْ لَهُمْ جُندٌ مُّحْضَرُونَ﴾.
That is, they worship them and undertake to support them, so they are to them like an army.
Qatāda said: they become angry on their behalf in this world.
And this is clear and good.
And it has been said: the explanation of this is what is related in the ḥadīth: (that for every people there will be made to appear what they used to worship besides Allah, Majestic and Mighty, and they will follow it into the Fire; so they are an army for them, brought into the Fire).

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلإِنسَانُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
Hushaym related from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: "al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil" took a decayed bone and crumbled it, and said: O Muḥammad, will Allah bring this to life after this? He said: Yes; Allah will cause you to die, then raise you, then put you into the fire of Hell. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلإِنسَانُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَاهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ فَإِذَا هُوَ خَصِيمٌ مُّبِينٌ. وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلاً وَنَسِيَ خَلْقَهُ قَالَ مَنْ يُحْيي العِِظَامَ وَهِيَ رَمِيمٌ﴾? to the end of the sūra.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: it was revealed about "Ubayy ibn Khalaf".
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says "the bone decayed (ramma)", so it is ramīm and rumām.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّجَرِ ٱلأَخْضَرِ نَاراً فَإِذَآ أَنتُم مِّنْه تُوقِدُونَ﴾.
It is the markh and the ʿafār [trees], from which the Bedouin make fire-sticks.

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿أَوَلَـيْسَ ٱلَذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاواتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ بِقَادِرٍ عَلَىٰ أَن يَخْلُقَ مِثْلَهُم بَلَىٰ﴾.
As He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿لَخَلْقُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ أَكْبَرُ مِنْ خَلْقِ النَّاسِ﴾.
And ﴿بَلَىٰ﴾ comes after a negation, and "نَعَمْ" may not be used [there]. If someone said to you "Did Zayd not stand?" and you said "Yes (naʿam)", the meaning would be reversed and become "yes, he did not stand"; but if you say "balā", the meaning is correct.
According to the Kufans it is "بَلْ" with a yāʾ added to it, because for them "بَلْ" is an affirmation after a negation; so it was chosen for this, and the yāʾ was added to it to indicate this meaning and to take it out of [its function as a conjunction of] sequence (nasaq).

nahhas-meani:83-83.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿فَسُبْحَانَ ٱلَّذِي بِيَدِهِ مَلَكُوتُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾.
That is, glorification [declaring free of imperfection] of the One in whose hand is the dominion of everything and its treasuries; so He is able to give life to the dead and [to do] whatever He wills.
﴿وَإِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ﴾: that is, you will be returned and come to Him after your death.
